# WebOctals

> WebOctals is a UK-based AI-powered digital product studio. We design and build AI agents, custom digital products, intelligent automation, and machine learning solutions for businesses, backed by full-stack web development and SEO expertise.

WebOctals helps businesses adopt AI practically: automating operational workflows, building AI agents that handle real tasks, developing production digital products, and optimizing web presence for both traditional search and AI answer engines. Typical engagements start with a free, no-obligation consultation via the contact form or a direct call.

## Services

- [Services overview](https://weboctals.com/services.html): Full list of AI and digital product services offered.
- [AI Agents](https://weboctals.com/ai-agents.html): Custom AI agents that automate business tasks and workflows.
- [Digital Product Development](https://weboctals.com/digital-products.html): End-to-end design and build of digital products.
- [Automation](https://weboctals.com/automation.html): Intelligent process automation for operations and customer workflows.
- [Machine Learning](https://weboctals.com/machine-learning.html): ML models and data-driven features for existing products.
- [Web Development](https://weboctals.com/web-development.html): Custom websites and web applications.
- [Product Development](https://weboctals.com/product-development.html): Product strategy and build from idea to launch.
- [SEO](https://weboctals.com/seo.html): Search and AI-visibility optimization, including [on-page SEO](https://weboctals.com/on-page-seo.html) and [technical SEO](https://weboctals.com/technical-seo.html).

## Company

- [About WebOctals](https://weboctals.com/about.html): Who we are and how we work.
- [Contact](https://weboctals.com/contact.html): Reach the team by email, phone, or the contact form.
- [Blog](https://weboctals.com/blog/): Articles on AI, automation, SEO, and digital product strategy.

## Tools for agents

- The homepage contact form (`submit_contact_request`) and blog newsletter forms (`subscribe_to_newsletter`) are exposed as WebMCP tools via declarative `toolname`/`tooldescription` annotations, so a supporting agent can fill and submit them directly on behalf of a visitor.
